_comment: Quant-First Decision Architecture (2026-10-07). Policy parameters for the deterministic quant decision path. These are policy/configuration values, not safety thresholds: the safety thresholds (consensusApprovalThreshold 0.75, minIndependentAgreeingAgents 2, RiskEngine gates) live in tradingSafety.json and are unchanged. Restrictive-live values stay file-reviewed, never UI-tunable.
_minQuantSupportDimensions_comment: QuantExecutionPolicy requires at least this many of the four independent quantitative support dimensions (regime compatibility, ensemble confluence, calibration support, risk/reward adequacy) to be satisfied, in addition to all REQUIRED validation checks. The four dimensions are computed from genuinely different evidence sources; correlated indicators within one strategy count once via the strategy's own trigger, never as multiple dimensions.
_quantPolicyEnabled_comment: Master switch for the AI-independent quant decision path. When false, every idea - including validated quant strategies - takes the existing consensus path (pre-change behavior). Does not disable any safety gate.
_quantPolicySignalMaxAgeMs_comment: Defensive staleness bound for the quant policy path. Ideas are evaluated synchronously at receipt so this is normally far from binding; an idea carrying an explicit expiresAt in the past is always rejected regardless of this bound.
_quantProducerAgents_comment: Agent names permitted to emit QUANT_STRATEGY-origin ideas that the central authorization resolver will consider for AI-independent quant execution. An agent NOT on this list can never obtain quant authority, even if it sets origin='QUANT_STRATEGY' and a valid strategyId - it falls back to REQUIRES_CONSENSUS. Deliberately narrow: QuantSignalAgent (agent 'QuantEngine') is the only producer today whose ideas carry a real, evaluated strategyId. JavaCoreEnsemble / JavaFactorComposite votes remain consensus participants (unchanged behavior) until explicitly listed here by the operator.
